title: Minimum tax on discretionary trusts
summary: A 30 per cent minimum tax on certain discretionary trust distributions from 1 July 2028 (announced in the 2026-27 Budget). Aims to make the tax system fairer and more sustainable. Does not apply to other types of trusts; some income types excluded.
notes: EXPOSURE DRAFT open for consultation 3-18 Sep 2026 (opened 3 Sep 2026). Draft instruments published on the consultation page: (1) exposure draft - minimum tax + imposition bill, with explanatory materials; (2) exposure draft - roll-over relief, with explanatory materials; (3) exposure draft - electable regime (exclusion from the minimum tax), with explanatory materials. Feedback sought on: how the minimum tax works; excluded types of trusts and income; definition of fixed trust; treatment of income tax-exempt entities; roll-over relief; the new electable regime; treatment of excess franking credits. Background: July 2026 consultation paper (c2026-784079). Contact: mintaxtrusts@treasury.gov.au.
commentary:
Exposure draft package (c2026-799771, closes 18 Sep 2026). Four instruments amend existing Acts:

1. **Minimum tax** (TLA Bill 2026 Sch 1): ITAA 1936 new ss 101AA–101AG + ITAA 1997 changes
2. **Imposition/rates** (ITRA Amendment Bill 2026): ITRA 1986 new s 12AB (30% rate) + s 28 rewrite
3. **Roll-over relief** (TLA Bill 2026): IT(TP)A 1997 new Subdiv 126-C (3-year restructuring window from 1 Jul 2027)
4. **Electable regime** (TLA Bill 2026): ITAA 1936 new Div 6F (EET election to opt out of the minimum tax for fixed-beneficiary trusts)

July 2026 consultation paper (c2026-784079) was background only.

sections.title: 101AA — Minimum tax trusts—trustees must pay a minimum amount of tax
sections.content:
If:
(a)	a trust estate has net income for a year of income; and
(b)	the trust estate is a minimum tax trust at the end of the year of income; and
(c)	the trustee is not assessed and is not liable under subsection 99A(4) or (4B) to pay tax on the net income;
the trustee of the trust estate is to be assessed and is liable to pay tax in respect of so much of the net income as is minimum tax income.

sections.title: 101AB — Minimum tax trusts—meaning of minimum tax trust
101AC — Minimum tax trusts—meaning of minimum tax income
sections.content: For a trust estate that is a minimum tax trust at the end of a year of income, the trust estate’s minimum tax income for the year of income is so much of the trust estate’s net income for the year of income as is not excluded by section 101AD or 101AE.

sections.title: 101AD — Minimum tax trusts—meaning of minimum tax income: excludes income from testamentary trusts
sections.content:
(1)	This section excludes from being minimum tax income any net income of a trust estate for a year of income that is derived from particular assessable income of the trust estate if:
(a)	the trust estate is established as a result of a will, codicil, order or intestacy as described in paragraph 102AG(2)(a); and
(b)	the assessable income concerned:
(i)	is of a kind covered by subsection 102AG(2AA) that is derived to benefit a beneficiary of the trust estate from property; or
(ii)	is otherwise derived to benefit a beneficiary of the trust estate from property transferred, before 7.30 pm by legal time in the Australian Capital Territory on 12 May 2026, to the trustee; and
(c)	if the trust estate is established on or after 1 July 2028—the beneficiary referred to in paragraph (b) of this subsection is:
(i)	an individual; or
(ii)	an exempt entity.
Note:	This exclusion only covers assessable income from trusts established and administered for genuine testamentary purposes (see subsections (2) and (3)).
(2)	Despite subsection (1), that subsection does not exclude net income of the trust estate if the net income was derived directly or indirectly under or as a result of a scheme that was entered into or carried out for the purpose, or for purposes that include the purpose, of causing subsection (1) to exclude the net income.
(3)	Despite subsection (1), that subsection does not exclude net income of the trust estate if the Commissioner is satisfied, having regard to the circumstances in which property is transferred to the trustee and any other relevant matters, that:
(a)	the net income is derived from property; and
(b)	the property, or property from which the property is ultimately derived (the original property), became property of the trustee as a result of a scheme; and
(c)	the scheme was entered into or carried out for the purpose, or for purposes that include the purpose, of:
(i)	causing the property, or the original property, to form part of the trust estate; and
(ii)	causing subsection (1) to exclude the net income.
(4)	In determining whether subsection (2) or (3) applies, disregard a purpose that is merely incidental.
(5)	In this section:
scheme has the same meaning as in the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997.

sections.title: 101AE — Minimum tax trusts—meaning of minimum tax income: other kinds of excluded income
sections.content:
(1)	This section excludes each of the following from being minimum tax income of a trust estate for a year of income:
(a)	taxable primary production income (within the meaning of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997);
(b)	a beneficiary’s share of the net income of the trust estate if:
(i)	the beneficiary is an individual who is less than 18 years of age on the last day of the year of income; and
(ii)	one or more of paragraphs 102AC(2)(c) to (g) (about vulnerable children) applies for the beneficiary for the year of income;
(c)	if a beneficiary of the trust estate is an individual who is less than 18 years of age on the last day of the year of income—so much of the beneficiary’s share of the net income of the trust estate as is derived as described in paragraph 102AG(2)(c);
(d)	a beneficiary’s share of the net income of the trust estate if:
(i)	the beneficiary is a registered charity, or a deductible gift recipient, on the last day of the year of income; and
(ii)	the conditions determined under paragraph (2)(a) are met;
(e)	if:
(i)	a beneficiary of the trust estate is an exempt entity, but neither a registered charity nor a deductible gift recipient, on the last day of the year of income; and
(ii)	the conditions determined under paragraph (2)(a) are met;
so much of the beneficiary’s share of the net income of the trust estate as meets the conditions determined under paragraph (2)(b);
(f)	so much of a beneficiary’s share of the net income of the trust estate as is a payment that:
(i)	is to a non-resident; and
(ii)	is a withholding payment (within the meaning of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997);
(g)	a part of the net income of the trust estate on which the trustee is to be assessed and is liable under subsection 99A(4A) or (4C) to pay tax.
(2)	The Minister may by legislative instrument:
(a)	determine conditions to be met for the purposes of subparagraph (1)(d)(ii) or (e)(ii); or
(b)	determine conditions to be met for working out how much of the shares of the net income of trust estates is not to be minimum tax income as the result of paragraph (1)(e).
(3)	For the purposes of (but without limiting subsection (2)):
(a)	a determination under paragraph (2)(a) may determine:
(i)	conditions to be met by or in relation to specified kinds of beneficiaries, trustees or trust estates; and
(ii)	conditions in the form of requirements, processes or integrity rules relating to paragraph (1)(d) or (e); and
(iii)	conditions requiring specified kinds of trustees to notify the Commissioner in the approved form of specified details relating to paragraph (1)(d) or (e); and
(b)	a determination under paragraph (2)(b) may determine:
(i)	a cap, or a method for working out a cap, on the total amount of the net income of specified kinds of trust estates that can be excluded by paragraph (1)(e) from being minimum tax income for a year of income; and
(ii)	a method for applying such a cap to work out the portion of the shares of specified kinds of beneficiaries of specified kinds of trust that is to be excluded by paragraph (1)(e) from being minimum tax income for a year of income.

sections.title: 101AF — Minimum tax trusts—tax offset for beneficiaries
sections.content:
(1)	An entity is entitled to a tax offset for a year of income if:
(a)	the entity is a beneficiary of a trust estate; and
(b)	the trustee is to be assessed and to be liable to pay tax under section 101AA in respect of so much of the net income of the trust estate for the year of income as is minimum tax income; and
(c)	under this Division, the beneficiary’s income for the year of income includes an amount (the beneficiary’s assessable amount) that is reasonably attributable to that minimum tax income; and
(d)	the beneficiary is not a body corporate.
(2)	The amount of the entity’s tax offset for the income year is equal to 30% of the beneficiary’s assessable amount.
Note:	The tax offset is not refundable.

sections.title: 101AG — Minimum tax trusts—reducing other rebates if minimum tax is payable by the trustee
sections.content:
(1)	A deduction or refund of tax (the rebate), to which a beneficiary of a trust estate is entitled under this Division, is reduced if:
(a)	the rebate is:
(i)	a deduction under paragraph 98A(2)(a) or subsection 98B(3) or 100(2); or
(ii)	a refund under subsection 99D(1); and
(b)	the rebate is in respect of tax (the primary tax) that the trustee is to be assessed and to be liable to pay:
(i)	under a provision of this Division other than section 99A or 101AA; and
(ii)	in respect of the whole, or a part, (the primary income) of the beneficiary’s share of the net income of the trust estate for a year of income; and
(c)	the trustee is to be assessed and to be liable to pay tax under section 101AA in respect of so much of the net income of the trust estate for the year of income as is minimum tax income; and
(d)	under this Division, the beneficiary’s income for the year of income includes an amount (the common amount) that is reasonably attributable to so much of that minimum tax income as is also primary income.
Note 1:	The beneficiary may be entitled to a tax offset under section 101AF relating to the tax payable by the trustee in respect of the common amount. This section removes any doubling up of rebate and tax offset for the common amount.
Note 2:	This section can apply to a beneficiary who is not entitled to a tax offset under section 101AF.
Note 3:	The reduction of the rebate does not affect any part of the rebate that is in respect of part of the primary income that is not common income.
Amount by which the rebate is reduced
(2)	If the trustee is to be so assessed and to be so liable to pay the primary tax at a rate that exceeds 30%, the rebate is reduced by the amount equal to 30% of the common income.
(3)	If the trustee is to be so assessed and to be so liable to pay the primary tax at a rate that does not exceed 30%, the rebate is reduced by the amount worked out by applying that rate to the common income.

sections.title: 102UW — Application of this Division
sections.content:
(1)	This Division applies if:
(a)	the net income of a trust estate for a year of income exceeds nil; and
(b)	any of the things mentioned in subsection (2) are taken into account in working out the net income of the trust estate for the year of income.
(2)	The things are as follows:
(a)	a capital gain, to the extent that an amount of the capital gain remains after applying steps 1 to 6 of the method statement in subsection 102-5(1) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997;
(b)	a franked distribution, to the extent that:
(i)	if the trust estate is a minimum tax trust at the end of the year of income—the franked distribution does not form part of the trust estate’s minimum tax income; and
(ii)	an amount of the franked distribution remains after reducing it by deductions directly relevant to it;
(c)	for a franking credit on a franked distribution, either:
(i)	unless subparagraph (ii) applies—all of the franking credit; or
(ii)	if the trust estate is a minimum tax trust at the end of the year of income—the proportion of the franking credit equal to the proportion of the franked distribution that does not form part of the trust estate’s minimum tax income.

sections.title: 272-65 — Fixed trust
102UYA — Excluded election trust
sections.content:
A minimum tax trust is an excluded election trust at any time when an EET election in respect of the trust is in force.
Note 1:	In order to be eligible for an election, the trust must be in existence on 1 July 2028 (see paragraph 102UYB(4)(a)).
Note 2:	See section 102UYH for when an election is in force.

sections.title: 102UYB — EET election and EET nomination
sections.content:
Nature of election
(1)	Subject to this section, the trustee of a minimum tax trust may make an election (the EET election) that the trust is an excluded election trust.
Nomination to accompany election and specify certain information
(2)	If the trustee makes an EET election in respect of the trust, a nomination (the EET nomination) specifying the following information must accompany the election:
(a)	each beneficiary to whom the trustee may confer a present entitlement to a share of both the income and capital of the trust for each year of income;
(b)	for each beneficiary specified under paragraph (a), the following for each year of income:
(i)	the beneficiary’s share of the income of the trust;
(ii)	the beneficiary’s share of the capital of the trust, which must equal the share specified in subparagraph (i);
(c)	the total of each share specified under paragraph (b), which may be conferred by the trustee to beneficiaries for each year of income, must equal 100% of the income and capital of the trust.
(3)	An entity must not be specified as a beneficiary in an EET nomination in respect of a trust if the entity:
(a)	unless section 102UYE (about variations) applies to the entity, was not an entity capable (whether by the exercise of a power of appointment or otherwise) of benefitting under the trust on 1 July 2028; or
(b)	is:
(i)	a complying superannuation entity; or
(ii)	a partnership; or
(iii)	a company unless it is an eligible company.
When an election can be made and requirement to notify the Commissioner
(4)	The trustee of a trust may make an EET election in respect of the trust if:
(a)	the trust is in existence on 1 July 2028; and
(b)	the election is made during the period:
(i)	starting on 1 July 2028; and
(ii)	ending on the last day of the first year of income of the trust that commences on or after 1 July 2028; and
(c)	notice of the election, and the accompanying nomination, is given in accordance with subsection (5).
(5)	The trustee must notify the Commissioner of the EET election, and an EET nomination that accompanies that election, in the approved form no later than the earlier of:
(a)	the due date for lodgment of the trust’s return of income for the year of income in which the election is made; and
(b)	the date of lodgment of the trust’s return of income for that year of income.
Trustee may only make one election and has not chosen to apply a roll-over
(6)	The trustee may not make an EET election in respect of a trust if:
(a)	the trustee has previously made an EET election in respect of the trust that has been revoked; or
(b)	a roll-over under Subdivision 126-C of the Income Tax (Transitional Provisions) Act 1997 applies in respect of the assets of the trust.
Note:	Subdivision 126-C of the Income Tax (Transitional Provisions) Act 1997 provides a transitional option for minimum tax trusts to restructure in response to the introduction of a minimum tax on those trusts and apply roll-over relief to assets transferred as part of that restructure.

sections.title: 102UYC — Eligible company
102UYD — Effect of an EET election
sections.content:
Taken not to be a minimum tax trust and related matters
(1)	At any time an EET election in respect of a trust is in force, and an EET nomination accompanies that election:
(a)	the trust is taken not to be a minimum tax trust for the purposes of this Act; and
(b)	for the purposes of Division 6, section 95A applies in relation to capital of the trust in the same way as it applies to income of the trust.
Note:	Paragraph (b) extends the operation of section 95A so that any deeming of present entitlement in respect of income of the trust under that section also applies to capital of the trust.
Trustee may act in accordance with EET nomination
(2)	If the trustee decides the EET election in respect of a trust is to be in force for a year of income, the trustee must confer present entitlements to shares of the income and capital of the trust in accordance with the EET nomination.
Note:	If the trustee decides not to act in accordance with the EET nomination as described in this subsection, this would result in an automatic revocation of the EET election (see paragraph 102UYF(2)(a)), meaning that the trust will again be a minimum tax trust for the purposes of this Act.

sections.title: 102UYE — Varying an EET nomination
sections.content:
Nominations generally cannot be varied
(1)	Subject to this section, an EET nomination that accompanies an EET election cannot be varied.
Variation—death of beneficiary
(2)	The trustee of an excluded election trust may, in respect of a year of income, vary the EET nomination so that one or more new individuals are specified for the purposes of subsection 102UYB(2) if:
(a)	an individual specified as a beneficiary under that subsection dies during the year of income; and
(b)	each new individual is a beneficiary of the deceased individual’s estate and either:
(i)	is a beneficiary already specified in the EET nomination; or
(ii)	is capable (whether by the exercise of a power of appointment or otherwise) of benefiting under the trust; and
(c)	the variation specifies each new individual as a beneficiary under paragraph 102UYB(2)(a) and specifies the information required under paragraph 102UYB(2)(b) for each new individual; and
(d)	the nomination, if varied, satisfies the requirement in paragraph 102UYB(2)(c); and
(e)	notice of the variation is given to the Commissioner in the approved form during the period within which the trustee is required to give to the Commissioner the trust’s return of income for the year of income in which the deceased individual dies.
Variation—relationship breakdown
(3)	The trustee of an excluded election trust may, in respect of a year of income, vary the EET nomination so that either or both of the following apply:
(a)	an individual specified in the nomination has a different share of the income and capital of the trust to what is specified in the nomination;
(b)	an individual specified in the nomination ceases to be specified in the nomination as a beneficiary of the trust.
(4)	A variation of an EET nomination under subsection (3) can only be made if:
(a)	one of the following:
(i)	an order;
(ii)	an agreement;
(iii)	an award;
of a kind mentioned in paragraphs 126-5(1)(a) to (f) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 involves 2 individuals who are beneficiaries specified in the EET nomination; and
(b)	as a result of the order, agreement or award:
(i)	if paragraph (3)(a) applies—each of the 2 beneficiaries has a different share of the income and capital of the trust to what is specified in the nomination; or
(ii)	if paragraph (3)(b) applies—one of the 2 individuals ceases to be an individual capable (whether by the exercise of a power of appointment or otherwise) of benefiting under the trust; and
(c)	the nomination, if so varied, satisfies the requirements in paragraphs 102UYB(2)(b) and (c); and
(d)	notice of the variation is given to the Commissioner in the approved form during the period within which the trustee is required to give to the Commissioner the trust’s return of income for the year of income in which the trustee decides or is required to give effect to the order, agreement or award.

sections.title: 102UYF — Revoking an EET election
sections.content:
How to revoke an EET election and requirement to notify the Commissioner
(1)	The trustee of an excluded election trust may revoke an EET election in respect of the trust if:
(a)	the trustee decides to do so before the end of a year of income for any future year of income; and
(b)	notice of the revocation is given to the Commissioner in the approved form no later than the earlier of:
(i)	the due date for lodgment of the trust’s return of income for the year of income in which the trustee decides to revoke the election; and
(ii)	the date of lodgment of the trust’s return of income for that year of income.
When an EET election is automatically revoked
(2)	An EET election in respect of an excluded election trust is automatically revoked if:
(a)	the trustee of the trust decides not to confer present entitlements in accordance with subsection 102UYD(2); or
(b)	a trust is specified as a beneficiary under an EET nomination accompanying the EET election and the trust vests in accordance with the trust deed or the trust estate is wound up; or
(c)	a company is specified as a beneficiary under an EET nomination accompanying the EET election, and the company:
(i)	is wound up; or
(ii)	is deregistered; or
(iii)	is no longer capable (whether by the exercise of a power of appointment or otherwise) of benefiting under the trust; or
(iv)	is no longer an eligible company; or
(d)	all of the following apply:
(i)	a company is specified as a beneficiary under an EET nomination accompanying the EET election;
(ii)	at the time the company is specified as a beneficiary under the EET nomination, an entity (within the meaning of section 960-100 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997) is the shareholder of a share in the company;
(iii)	the entity ceases to be the shareholder of that share for a reason other than a reason (an allowable reason) set out in subsection (3).
(3)	Each of the following is an allowable reason:
(a)	the entity is an individual and the individual dies;
(b)	the entity is an individual and one of the following:
(i)	an order;
(ii)	an agreement;
(iii)	an award;
of a kind mentioned in paragraphs 126-5(1)(a) to (f) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 involves the individual and, as a result of the order, agreement or award, the individual ceases to be the shareholder of that share.

sections.title: 102UYG — Effect of an EET election being revoked
sections.content:
(1)	This section applies if an EET election in respect of an excluded election trust is revoked under section 102UYF in a year of income.
(2)	Any accompanying EET nomination is taken to be revoked at the same time.
(3)	If, apart from this section, a beneficiary of the trust is presently entitled to either or both of the following (the relevant share) in respect of the year of income:
(a)	a share of the income of the trust;
(b)	a share of the capital of the trust;
then, for the purposes of this Act, the beneficiary, is taken not to be, and taken never to have been, presently entitled to the relevant share in respect of the year of income.
(4)	Division 6 applies in relation to the trust and the year of income as if:
(a)	subsections 99A(2) to (3A) were not enacted; and
(b)	the trust estate were a resident trust estate.
Note:	For the year of income an EET election is revoked, any present entitlements of a share of income or capital of the trust conferred by the trustee of a trust are deemed not to be effective. Those shares are therefore assessable in respect of the trustee of the trust as undistributed trust income under Division 6.

sections.title: 102UYH — When an EET election is in force
sections.content:
(1)	An EET election, in respect of a trust, is in force:
(a)	if it is not revoked—at all times after the start of the year of income in which the trustee made the election; or
(b)	if it is revoked under subsection 102UYF(1)—at all times during the period:
(i)	starting at the start of the year of income in which the trustee made the election; and
(ii)	ending at the end of the year of income in which the trustee of the trust decides to revoke the election; or
(c)	if it is automatically revoked under subsection 102UYF(2)—at all times during the period:
(i)	starting at the start of the year of income in which the trustee made the election; and
(ii)	ending at the end of the year of income immediately before the year of income in which the election is so revoked.
(2)	Any accompanying EET nomination is taken to be in force at all times that the EET election is in force.

sections.title: 12AB — Rate of tax on minimum tax income of minimum tax trusts
28 — Rates of tax payable by certain trustees to whom section 98 or 101AA of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936 applies
sections.content:
(1)	The rates of tax payable by a trustee of a trust estate in respect of a beneficiary’s share of the net income of the trust estate in respect of which the trustee is to be assessed and is liable to pay tax are:
(a)	if:
(i)	paragraph 98(3)(b) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936 applies; and
(ii)	the beneficiary is a company to which paragraph 23(2)(a) of this Act applies;
the rate specified in subsection (2) of this section; or
(b)	if:
(i)	paragraph 98(3)(b) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936 applies; and
(ii)	the beneficiary is a company to which paragraph 23(2)(b) of this Act applies;
the rate specified in subsection (3) of this section; or
(c)	if subsection 98(4) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936 applies—the rate specified in subsection (4) of this section.
Note:	Paragraph 98(3)(b) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936 is about beneficiaries that are companies. Subsection 98(4) of that Act is about beneficiaries that are themselves trustees jointly with other entities that are non-residents.
(2)	For the purposes of paragraph (1)(a):
(a)	to the extent that section 101AA of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936 applies to the trust estate for so much of the share of the net income as is minimum tax income—the rate (for the purposes of that section) is 30%; and
(b)	otherwise—the rate (for the purposes of paragraph 98(3)(b) of that Act) is the same as the rate specified in paragraph 23(2)(a) of this Act.
Note:	This means the rate specified in paragraph 23(2)(a) applies:
(a)	if paragraph (a) of this subsection applies—to so much of the share of the net income as is not minimum tax income; or
(b)	otherwise—to all of the share of the net income.
(3)	For the purposes of paragraph (1)(b):
(a)	the rate (for the purposes of paragraph 98(3)(b) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936) is the same as the rate specified in paragraph 23(2)(b) of this Act; and
(b)	the rate (for the purposes of section 101AA of that Act (if applicable)) is nil.
Note:	This means the rate specified in paragraph 23(2)(b) applies to all of the share of the net income.
(4)	For the purposes of paragraph (1)(c):
(a)	the rate (for the purposes of subsection 98(4) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936) is the same as the maximum rate specified in column 3 of the table applicable to the year of income in Part II of Schedule 7 to this Act that applies for the year of income; and
(b)	the rate (for the purposes of section 101AA of that Act (if applicable)) is nil.
Note:	This means the rate referred to in paragraph (a) applies to all of the share of the net income.

sections.title: 126-425 — Object of this Subdivision
sections.content:
Following the introduction of a minimum tax on minimum tax trusts, the object of this Subdivision is to provide transitional relief for a 3-year period to facilitate flexibility for trustees of such trusts to restructure the trust, and the way the trust’s assets are held, while disregarding tax gains and losses that would otherwise arise.
Note:	For the minimum tax on minimum tax trusts see sections 101AA to 101AG of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936.

sections.title: 126-430 — When a roll-over is available
126-431 — Choosing roll-over relief
sections.content:
Transferors
(1)	The choice by the transferor under paragraph 126-430(1)(c) must:
(a)	be made in the approved form; and
(b)	specify the entity that is to be the transferee for the assets of the minimum tax trust in relation to the restructure; and
(c)	be given to the Commissioner by the earlier of:
(i)	the day the transferor lodges the transferor’s income tax return for the income year in which the first asset transfer of the restructure occurs; and
(ii)	the day on which that income tax return is due to be lodged;
or within such further time as the Commissioner allows.
(2)	The choice cannot be revoked.
(3)	The choice cannot be made if the transferor, as trustee of the minimum tax trust, has already made an excluded election trust election (within the meaning of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936) in relation to the trust.
(4)	The transferor cannot make more than one choice under subsection (1) in relation to the minimum tax trust.
Transferees
(5)	The choice by the transferee under paragraph 126-430(1)(c) must:
(a)	be made in the approved form; and
(b)	in the case of a transferee that is a partnership—be made by each partner of the partnership to whom an asset is transferred under the restructure; and
(c)	be given to the Commissioner by the earlier of:
(i)	the day the transferee lodges the transferee’s income tax return for the income year in which the first asset transfer of the restructure occurs; and
(ii)	the day on which that income tax return is due to be lodged;
or within such further time as the Commissioner allows.
(6)	The choice cannot be revoked.

sections.title: 126-432 — Notifying the Commissioner of progress of restructure
sections.content:
(1)	The requirement for the purposes of paragraph 126-430(1)(d) is that, if the asset is transferred in any income year (the later income year) after the income year in which the first asset transfer of the restructure occurred, the transferor must have notified the Commissioner that the restructure is in progress.
(2)	The notice must be:
(a)	in the approved form; and
(b)	given to the Commissioner no later than the day the income tax return for the minimum tax trust for the later income year is lodged.

sections.title: 126-433 — Notifying the Commissioner if restructure not completed or roll-over condition not met
sections.content:
(1)	If:
(a)	the transferor and transferee make a choice for roll-over relief under this Subdivision to apply in relation to a restructure of a minimum tax trust; and
(b)	either or both of the following apply:
(i)	the transferor does not transfer all of the relevant assets of the trust required to avoid a roll-over becoming unavailable because of subsection 126-430(3);
(ii)	the transferor or transferee fails to satisfy any other condition of a roll-over being available under this Subdivision in relation to the restructure;
the transferor and transferee must each notify the Commissioner.
(2)	The notice must be:
(a)	in the approved form; and
(b)	given to the Commissioner by the earlier of:
(i)	the day the transferor or transferee (as the case requires) lodges their income tax return for the income year in which the relevant event in subparagraph (1)(b)(i) or (ii) occurs; or
(ii)	the day on which that income tax return is due to be lodged;
or within such further time as the Commissioner allows.

sections.title: 126-440 — Continuity requirements
sections.content:
Family trusts
(1)	For the purposes of paragraph 126-430(1)(e), if the minimum tax trust of which the transferor is trustee is a family trust, the continuity requirements for the transaction are:
(a)	if the transferee is an entity other than an individual—every individual who, just after the transaction takes effect, has a direct or indirect interest in the transferee must, just before the transaction took effect, have been:
(i)	a beneficiary under the family trust; and
(ii)	a member of the family group (within the meaning of Schedule 2F to the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936) relating to the family trust; and
(b)	if the transferee is an individual—the transferee must, just before the transaction took effect, have been a beneficiary and member as described in subparagraphs (a)(i) and (ii) in relation to the family trust.
Other trusts
(2)	For the purposes of paragraph 126-430(1)(e), if the minimum tax trust of which the transferor is trustee is not a family trust, the continuity requirements for the transaction are the requirements determined under subsection (3).
(3)	The Minister may, by legislative instrument, determine requirements for the purposes of subsection (2).
(4)	To avoid doubt, if no determination of requirements under subsection (3) is in force, subsection (2) does not apply.

sections.title: 126-445 — Residency requirement
sections.content:
For the purposes of paragraph 126-430(1)(f), the residency requirement for an entity is that:
(a)	if the entity is an individual or a company—the entity is an Australian resident; or
(b)	if the entity is a trust—it is a resident trust for CGT purposes; or
(c)	if the entity is a partnership (other than a corporate limited partnership)—each partner to whom an asset is transferred is an Australian resident; or
(d)	if the entity is a corporate limited partnership—it is, under section 94T of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936, a resident for the purposes of the income tax law.

sections.title: 126-450 — Minimum tax trust restructure transfers not to affect income tax positions
sections.content:
(1)	Except as provided by this Subdivision, a transfer of an asset has no direct consequences under the income tax law if:
(a)	the transfer occurs under a transaction in relation to which section 126-430 applies; and
(b)	a roll-over under this Subdivision is available under that section in relation to the asset.
(2)	To avoid doubt, this section does not affect the application of the income tax law in relation to:
(a)	anything that happens in relation to the asset that does not directly relate to the transfer; or
(b)	the ownership of the asset at any time.

sections.title: 126-451 — Minimum tax trust restructure transfers not to result in family trust distribution tax
sections.content:
A transfer of an asset does not result in any family trust distribution tax under sections 271-15 to 271-30 of Schedule 2F to the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936 if:
(a)	the transfer occurs under a transaction in relation to which section 126-430 applies; and
(b)	a roll-over under this Subdivision is available under that section in relation to the asset.

sections.title: 126-455 — Effect of minimum tax trust restructures on transferred cost of assets
126-456 — Effect of minimum tax trust restructures—depreciating assets
sections.content:
If section 126-455 applies in relation to the transfer of a depreciating asset under a transaction:
(a)	paragraph 40-340(1)(c) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 is taken to be satisfied for the purposes of section 40-340 of that Act applying to the transfer; and
(b)	paragraph 328-243(1A)(c) of that Act (as affected by subsection 40-340(2) of that Act) is taken to be satisfied for the purposes of subsection 328-243(1A) of that Act applying to the transfer.
Note 1:	Section 40-340 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 provides for roll-over relief in relation to a disposal of a depreciating asset in certain circumstances.
Note 2:	Subsection 328-243(1A) of that Act applies the roll-over relief available under subsection 40-340(1) of that Act to small business assets.

sections.title: 126-465 — New membership interests as consideration for transfer of assets
sections.content:
(1)	If:
(a)	section 126-455 applies in relation to the transfer of an asset under a transaction; and
(b)	the transaction provides for membership interests to be issued; and
(c)	the membership interests constitute all or part of the consideration provided for the transfer of assets (transferred assets) under the transaction;
then:
(d)	the first element of the membership interests’ cost base is the sum of:
(i)	the roll-over costs of the transferred assets that are not depreciating assets; and
(ii)	the adjustable values of the transferred assets that are depreciating assets;
(less any liabilities that a transferee of any of the transferred assets undertakes to discharge in respect of the transferred assets) divided by the number of membership interests; and
(e)	the first element of the membership interests’ reduced cost base is worked out similarly.
(2)	However, if the membership interests constituted only a part of the total consideration provided for the transfer of the transferred assets, reduce accordingly the amounts worked out under paragraphs (1)(d) and (e).

sections.title: 126-470 — Membership interests affected by transfers of assets
sections.content:
If:
(a)	section 126-455 applies in relation to the transfer of an asset under a transaction; and
(b)	an entity holds, either directly or indirectly:
(i)	a membership interest in the transferor or a transferee; or
(ii)	a membership interest that was issued as provided for by the transaction;
disregard a capital loss from a CGT event that arises in relation to the membership interest after the transaction takes effect, except to the extent that the entity can demonstrate that the loss is attributable to a matter other than the transaction.

sections.title: 126-475 — Restructures involving assets already subject to small business roll-over
sections.content:
(1)	If:
(a)	section 126-455 applies in relation to the transfer of an asset (the transferred asset) of the transferor to one or more transferees; and
(b)	the transferor has previously chosen a small business roll-over under Subdivision 152-E of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 for a CGT event that happened in relation to a CGT asset for which the transferred asset is a replacement asset (within the meaning of sections 104-185, 104-190, 104-197 and 104-198 of that Act);
sections 104-185, 104-190, 104-197 and 104-198 of that Act apply to each transferee (to the extent of the transferee’s interest in the asset) as if the transferee, and not the transferor, made that choice.
Note:	Sections 104-185, 104-190, 104-197 and 104-198 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 provide for capital gains to arise under CGT events J2, J5 and J6, after the choice of a small business roll-over under Subdivision 152-E has deferred the making of a capital gain.
(2)	However, if a transferee is a partnership, subsection (1) applies as if:
(a)	the words “to each transferee (to the extent of the transferee’s interest in the asset) as if the transferee” were omitted; and
(b)	the words “to each partner of the partnership (to the extent of the partner’s interest in the asset) as if the partner” were substituted.

sections.title: 126-480 — Continuing time periods for assets transferred under the roll-over
sections.content:
If section 126-450 or 126-455 applies in relation to the transfer of an asset to the transferee, then paragraphs 152-105(b) and (c) and 152-110(1)(b) and (c) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 (the 15-year and significant individual rules) apply as if:
(a)	the transferee had acquired the asset when the transferor acquired it; or
(b)	in a case where, for the purposes of applying those paragraphs, the time when the transferor acquired the asset was provided for by this section—the transferee had acquired the asset at that time.
